claims.text: Controlled isothermal aging combined with optimized Cu content will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates in a CoCrFeNiMn-based high-entropy alloy.
The Cu-rich precipitates will enhance heat-transfer capability by approximately 20–30% relative to untreated material.
The proposed treatment will preserve or improve mechanical strength under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
The initial material is a CoCrFeNiMn-based high-entropy alloy with a minor Cu addition in an as-cast or as-solutionized state.
The proposed aging treatment is approximately 700°C for 2–4 hours followed by controlled cooling.
Adjusting Cu content or adding minor alloying elements can fine-tune precipitate size and interfacial properties.
The hypothesized performance range is 500–700°C under cyclic mechanical loading representative of plasma-facing reactor environments.
The treatment will yield Cu-rich precipitates that are coherent or semi-coherent with the matrix.
An optimized precipitate size distribution will minimize precipitate–matrix thermal-interface resistance.
Cu-rich precipitates provide localized pathways for electron and phonon transport and thereby act as thermal bridges.
Coherent Cu-rich precipitates cause precipitation strengthening.
Precipitation strengthening will maintain or improve structural integrity at high temperature under cyclic loading.
Fine-tuning Cu content mitigates precipitate coarsening and excessive thermal-interface resistance.
The treated alloy will exhibit a 20–30% increase in thermal conductivity relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will retain or improve mechanical strength during cyclic loading at 500–700°C.
Untreated CoCrFeNiMn-based alloy with minor Cu addition has lower thermal conductivity and mechanical performance under plasma-facing conditions.
High precipitate–matrix thermal-interface resistance may limit the proposed conductivity improvement.
Non-optimal aging parameters or Cu content may cause precipitate coarsening.
